steps.tx: Malignancy induces a prothrombotic state via tumour cell procoagulants, inflammatory cytokines, and vascular stasis. The **Khorana risk score** stratifies **venous thromboembolism** VTE risk in ambulatory cancer patients initiating chemotherapy based on cancer site, platelet, leukocyte, and haemoglobin counts, and BMI. Very high-risk cancer sites (stomach, pancreas) receive 2 points, while high-risk sites (lung, lymphoma, gynaecologic, bladder, testicular) receive 1 point.

steps.tx: Pivotal trials established low molecular weight heparin as superior to oral vitamin K antagonists in oncology. Low molecular weight heparin LMWH **dalteparin** proved superior to oral vitamin K antagonists in reducing recurrent VTE without excess bleeding in cancer patients in the **CLOT trial**. Dalteparin 200 units/kg once daily for one month followed by 150 units/kg daily halved the rate of recurrent thromboembolism compared to warfarin without increasing major haemorrhage.

Dalteparin 200 units per kilogram once daily for one month followed by 150 units per kilogram daily halved the rate of recurrent thromboembolism compared to warfarin without increasing major haemorrhage.

left.title: Low Molecular Weight Heparin (Dalteparin)
points: CLOT trial: 52% relative risk reduction in recurrent VTE (p=0.002)
Predictable weight-based subcutaneous pharmacokinetics
Zero interference from nausea, vomiting, or malabsorption
Rapid onset and offset allows flexible interruption for procedures

right.title: Vitamin K Antagonists (Warfarin)
points: Narrow therapeutic window (INR 2.0 to 3.0)
Unpredictable fluctuations due to liver disease and chemotherapy interactions
High rates of both subtherapeutic thrombosis and fatal bleeding
No longer recommended as first-line therapy in cancer-associated thrombosis

steps.tx: Direct oral anticoagulants provide non-inferior oral alternatives to parenteral low molecular weight heparin. **Direct oral anticoagulants** DOACs apixaban, edoxaban, and rivaroxaban are approved first-line alternatives to LMWH for cancer-associated thrombosis in the **CARAVAGGIO**, Hokusai VTE Cancer, and SELECT-D trials. In the CARAVAGGIO trial, oral apixaban demonstrated non-inferiority to subcutaneous dalteparin for recurrent VTE without increasing major gastrointestinal bleeding.

rows: Apixaban 10 mg BID for 7 days, then 5 mg BID
VTE recurrence 5.6% vs 7.9% (non-inferior); major GI bleeding similar (1.9% vs 1.7%)
Non-inferior for recurrent VTE; higher major GI bleeding in luminal GI tumours
Rivaroxaban 15 mg BID for 3 weeks, then 20 mg daily
Lower VTE recurrence (4% vs 11%); increased mucosal GI and GU bleeding

steps.tx: Luminal gastrointestinal and genitourinary neoplasms carry heightened bleeding risks that restrict direct oral anticoagulant selection. Oral DOACs carry an increased risk of **gastrointestinal** and genitourinary **mucosal bleeding** compared to LMWH in patients with unresected luminal gastrointestinal or urothelial tumours. In intact oesophageal, gastric, or duodenal malignancies, local mucosal ulceration exposed to unabsorbed oral anticoagulant promotes severe haemorrhage, making LMWH the preferred agent.

left.title: Indications Preferring LMWH
points: Unresected luminal upper GI malignancies (oesophageal, gastric, pancreatic)
Active gastrointestinal ulcerations or mucosal lesions
Unresected urothelial carcinomas at risk of gross haematuria
Severe drug-drug interactions with strong P-gp / CYP3A4 inhibitors
Severe renal impairment with CrCl < 30 mL/min

right.title: Indications Suitable for DOACs
points: Solid tumours without intact luminal GI ulceration (breast, lung, prostate)
Resected gastrointestinal cancers with no residual mucosal primary
Haematologic malignancies (lymphoma, myeloma) without mucosal lesions
Patients with severe needle phobia or LMWH-induced bruising

steps.tx: Prophylactic oral anticoagulation significantly prevents venous thromboembolism in high-risk ambulatory outpatients initiating chemotherapy. Primary **thromboprophylaxis** with oral apixaban 2.5 mg twice daily or rivaroxaban 10 mg daily significantly reduces VTE in intermediate-to-high risk outpatients with **Khorana score** 2 or higher in AVERT and CASSINI. In the AVERT trial, apixaban reduced symptomatic VTE from 10.2% to 4.2% (hazard ratio 0.41), with low rates of major bleeding.

nodes.label: Screen: Rule Out Active Luminal Bleeding & CrCl < 30
Initiate Oral Apixaban 2.5 mg BID or Rivaroxaban 10 mg QD
Halves Incidence of Symptomatic Pulmonary Embolism & DVT

steps.tx: **Primary thromboprophylaxis** is reserved for hospitalised or ambulatory cancer patients at high risk, with bleeding risk assessed first. Mechanical prophylaxis is used when anticoagulation is contraindicated, such as active bleeding or platelets below 50,000/mcL. After major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery, prophylaxis may be extended up to four weeks. Watch for the fall in platelets with heparin, which needs review.
steps.say: Primary thromboprophylaxis is reserved for hospitalised or ambulatory cancer patients at high risk, after bleeding risk is assessed. Mechanical prophylaxis is used when anticoagulation is contraindicated, such as active bleeding or platelets below 50,000 per microlitre. After major abdominal or pelvic cancer surgery, prophylaxis may be extended for up to four weeks.

steps.tx: Central venous access devices are frequent sites of thrombosis managed without routine line sacrifice. **Catheter-related thrombosis** is managed with **therapeutic anticoagulation** without mandatory catheter removal if the line remains well-positioned, functional, and non-infected. Anticoagulation with LMWH or DOAC is continued for at least three months and as long as the catheter remains in situ; removal is reserved for catheter infection, line malfunction, or progressive clot despite anticoagulation.

steps.tx: Asymptomatic thromboembolic events discovered on restaging scans require identical full-dose therapeutic management. **Incidental asymptomatic** pulmonary embolism detected on staging contrast-enhanced CT scans carries clinical outcomes comparable to symptomatic PE, warranting identical **therapeutic anticoagulation**. Autopsy and clinical registry series demonstrate equivalent risks of fatal clot recurrence and mortality between incidental segmental/subsegmental emboli and clinically symptomatic presentations.

left.title: Incidental Asymptomatic Pulmonary Embolism
points: Detected unexpectedly on routine contrast-enhanced restaging CT
Present in up to 5% of all contrast-enhanced staging examinations
Affects segmental, lobar, or main pulmonary arteries
Requires full-dose therapeutic LMWH or DOAC identical to symptomatic PE

right.title: Symptomatic Acute Pulmonary Embolism
points: Presents with acute dyspnoea, pleuritic chest pain, or tachycardia
Investigated intentionally with dedicated CT pulmonary angiography
Risk of acute right ventricular strain and obstructive shock
Requires therapeutic anticoagulation and hemodynamic resuscitation

steps.tx: Anticoagulation duration in cancer-associated thrombosis is determined by active malignancy status and therapy. **Cancer-associated thrombosis** anticoagulation is recommended for a **minimum duration** of 6 months, continuing indefinitely while active cancer or active anticancer therapy is ongoing. Discontinuation after six months in the presence of active metastatic disease or ongoing systemic therapy results in a recurrent thrombosis rate exceeding thirty percent within twelve months.
